sub_answers.text: The promotion sent talent to participate in NJPW's Wrestle Kingdom events and accepted NJPW talent for excursions, exemplified by Kazuchika Okada being sent on a training excursion to the promotion before becoming a future IWGP Heavyweight Champion [d454401s16p0]. The promotion’s working agreements have allowed its championships and wrestlers to be defended and appear on partner shows, increasing those wrestlers' visibility across partner promotions' audiences [d454401s16p0]. The promotion’s talent exchange with AAA and Lucha Underground enabled cross-appearances that led to co-promoted supershows and sell-out crowds, widening roster exposure internationally [d454401s16p0].

sub_answers.text: Promotional storylines have integrated allied fighters and managers who back talent on-screen and form named alliances that compete on cards, as when Junior dos Santos backed Dan Lambert and allied fighters to form an alliance with Men of the Year in AEW [d19940888s10p0]. Groups can be officially added to a promotion's roster and use interference and assaults to create title opportunities and storyline momentum, as The Academy did in the IWA before being included on the roster and pursuing championships [d30298227s2p0]. Factions have been part of multi-person matches and trios bouts on major cards, exemplified by Dos Santos teaming with Scorpio Sky and Ethan Page in a trios match on AEW Rampage [d19940888s10p0].

sub_answers.text: Promotions have used single-elimination tournaments to crown inaugural champions, such as the four-woman single-elimination tournament to determine the inaugural Strong Women's Champion [d73664096s1p0]. Tag title tournaments and multi-competitor Royal Rumble–style matches have been used in tournament structures, as seen in an NWA Wildside Tag Team Championship tournament that included a Royal Rumble–style handicap mega match in round one [d68426977s12p0]. Promotions also hold recurring themed events that feature title matches and contender angles, for example annual events like IWA's Halloween Mayhem and season-closing Christmas shows used to stage championship angles [d30298227s2p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How has the promotion historically handled sudden roster changes (injuries, departures) in terms of booking adjustments?
sub_answers.text: Promotions have booked around sudden injuries by adjusting title status and match bookings, including an angle where an incumbent champion was portrayed as injured, the title was briefly forfeited and awarded to a challenger, then the decision was later revoked and a replacement match held to resolve the championship situation [d30298227s2p0].

sub_answers.text: TNA/Impact co-promoted with Hermie Sadler's United Wrestling Federation (United States) under a 2006 agreement allowing UWF to use the TNA logo and six-sided ring, with the TNA name agreement ending at the end of 2006 [d454401s16p0]. TNA worked with Mexico's Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) from 2007 to 2009 and later established a working agreement with Mexico's Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (AAA) since 2015, including co-promotion of the Ultra Clash supershow in the Monterrey area on November 26, 2023 [d454401s16p0]. TNA/Impact partnered with Japan's New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) initially from 2008 to 2011 and re-established the relationship in February 2021 which lasted until December 2024, during which TNA sent talent to NJPW Wrestle Kingdom events and NJPW sent Kazuchika Okada on a TNA training excursion [d454401s16p0]. On March 2, 2014 TNA collaborated with Japan's Wrestle-1 to produce the Kaisen: Outbreak supershow in Tokyo where three TNA championships were defended, and that Wrestle-1 relationship ended by May 2015 [d454401s16p0]. Impact maintained working relationships with Japan's Inoki Genome Federation (IGF), Pro Wrestling Noah, Wrestle-1, and with U.S. promotions including the original Global Force Wrestling, OMEGA Championship Wrestling, Evolve Wrestling, and from December 2020 had a partnership with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) until October 2021 [d454401s16p0]. Impact established broader co-promotion arrangements since 2018 with numerous regional/independent promotions for house shows, Twitch specials, and Impact Plus events including Future Stars of Wrestling, Smash Wrestling, AML Wrestling, Border City Wrestling, WrestleCade, Rocky Mountain Pro, Rockstar Pro Wrestling, Wrestlepro, Wrestling Revolver, RISE, Destiny Wrestling, Big Time Wrestling (California), DEFY Wrestling and House of Hardcore [d454401s16p0]. Impact announced widening talent exchanges with WWE starting in 2024, including appearances on WWE NXT, and WWE announced a multi-year partnership on January 16, 2025 to allow cross-appearances on NXT, iMPACT!, select WWE Premium Live Events and TNA pay-per-views [d454401s16p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide concrete examples of talent-exchange deals, loaned wrestler appearances, or organized international tours involving the 2001-founded promotion, and explain how each instance changed the visibility of individual wrestlers or altered career trajectories (e.g., new contracts, title wins, bookings, TV exposure, or signing by larger promotions).
sub_answers.text: NJPW sent Kazuchika Okada on a training excursion to TNA, and Okada later became IWGP Heavyweight Champion, linking the TNA stint to a subsequent rise in Okada's profile in NJPW [d454401s16p0]. AEW and Impact ran a talent/title-exchange partnership beginning in December 2020 that placed AEW wrestlers and titles on Impact programming, increasing cross-exposure of talent between the two promotions until the relationship ended in October 2021 [d454401s16p0]. Impact's Knockouts Champion Mickie James entered WWE's 2022 Royal Rumble match with WWE's account and Impact recognizing her as Impact champion, providing WWE TV exposure to an Impact titleholder [d454401s16p0]. In 2024 Impact and WWE broadened a talent exchange allowing several Impact/TNA wrestlers to appear on WWE NXT and NXT wrestlers to appear at TNA events, creating reciprocal TV exposure across promotions [d454401s16p0].
